Calibrate a test result with a null model

Source: R/null_models.R
calibrate.Rd

Refers the statistics of a test() or test_measure() result to a null model: the adjusted statistic \((z - \mathrm{null\_mean}) / \mathrm{null\_sd}\) replaces the standard normal in the p-values and flags, and the confidence limits are those of the inverted calibrated test, \(\hat\theta - (\mathrm{null\_mean} \pm c\, \mathrm{null\_sd})\, se\), so that a limit excludes the null value exactly when the provider is flagged.

Usage

calibrate(
  x,
  null_model,
  level = NULL,
  alternative = NULL,
  critical = NULL,
  ci_location = NULL
)

Arguments

x

a test result.

null_model

a pp_null object, or a function of x returning one (for instance function(t) null_model("empirical", t, n_groups = 4)).

level, alternative

default to the settings of x.

critical

optional critical value for the flags and limits instead of the normal quantile for level.

ci_location

location at which the confidence limits are centred: NULL (default) uses the null mean, so that a limit excludes the null value exactly when the provider is flagged; a number or one value per provider centres the limits elsewhere, for instance 0 for limits of the form \(\hat\theta \pm c\, \mathrm{null\_sd}\, se\) that ignore the null location.

Value

x with the columns z_adjusted, null_mean, null_sd and null_group added, p and flag recomputed from the adjusted statistic, and lower/upper recomputed where a standard error is available (for test_measure() results on the transformed scale, mapped back; for the log-ratio Wald and mid-p tests of test.cox() on the ratio scale, the mid-p limits by root finding); the settings are recorded in the test attribute. The exact Poisson test cannot be calibrated.

Examples

d <- sim_kecc(n_providers = 40, seed = 1)
pd <- pp_data(d, y = "y", x = c("x1", "x2", "x3"), provider = "provider",
              patient = "patient", message = FALSE)
tst <- test(fit_logistic_fe(pd), statistic = "wald", variance = "robust")
calibrate(tst, null_model("fixed", sd = 1.5))
#> Provider tests: wald statistic, robust variance; null median = -0.965; two.sided, level 0.95
#>   40 providers: 6 above, 4 below, 30 not different, 0 not tested

#>      P004  -1.9726 0.2968     -0.965   -3.3953    -2.2636         0     1.5
